race_context: Loogootee Community School Corporation serves Loogootee in Martin County, Indiana, with three schools: Loogootee Elementary, Loogootee Middle and Loogootee High {loog_enroll}{nces_loog}. Federal data reported through PlainSchools show 762 students in 2024-25 {nces_loog}. The district describes itself as the smallest district in the country to offer the Project Lead the Way curriculum in grades K-12 {loog_enroll}.
The district's staff directory lists Dr. Shelley Christmas as superintendent {loog_dir}.

The board has five members: Brent Courter, Dr. Brooke Hawkins, TJ McAtee, Nick Toy and Chad Wade; the district says officers were chosen by the board on Jan. 15, 2026, and it lists McAtee as president, Toy as vice president and Courter as secretary {loog_board}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the state list shows one race, 'Martin Loogootee Community School, At Large (3 seats)', in which voters choose up to three of seven candidates {in_list}{incitizen_list}. The three seats last on the ballot were filled in 2022, when Nick Toy (District 1), Chad Wade (District 2) and Brent Courter (District 3) were unopposed and were elected to new four-year terms {wth_2022}. Of those three, only Toy appears to be on the 2026 ballot (as Nicholas Toy); Wade and Courter are not listed {in_list}{wth_early}.

Seat design: in 2022 the Times Herald listed the Loogootee seats by district number {wth_2022}, while the 2026 state list labels the race 'At Large (3 seats)' {in_list}. This guide could not confirm whether the district numbers are residency districts or whether the seat structure changed.

Budget and referendums: Loogootee is not on the Indiana Department of Local Government Finance's list of school districts with referendums on the November 2026 ballot {dlgf_ref}. The district's public-hearing page listed no pending hearings when this guide checked {loog_hearings}. This guide found no news coverage of the board's 2025-26 decisions on the budget, the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1), facilities or curriculum.
Forums: this guide found no candidate forum, questionnaire or voter guide for this race. The Washington Times Herald listed the seven candidates in its Oct. 7, 2026 early-voting article {wth_early}.
